questions.q: How did Genghis Khan build and organise the Mongol Empire?

answer.text: Genghis Khan, originally named Temujin, rose from a difficult childhood to unite the warring nomadic tribes of the Mongol steppe. In 1206 an assembly of Mongol chieftains, called a quriltai, proclaimed him the Great Khan, the supreme ruler of all the Mongols.

He built a highly disciplined army organised on the decimal system, in units of ten, hundred, thousand and ten thousand, the last called a tumen. Old tribal loyalties were broken up and soldiers were mixed across units, so that loyalty was to the Khan alone. His mounted archers were swift, mobile and deadly.
With this army he conquered northern China, Central Asia and Iran, creating the beginnings of the largest land empire in history.

answer: His genius in war and organisation laid the foundation of Mongol power.

questions.q: How did the Mongols govern and connect their vast empire?
answer: Once conquered, the huge Mongol empire had to be governed and held together, and the Mongols proved capable rulers as well as conquerors.

answer.text: The Mongols were few in number compared with the peoples they ruled, so they often adopted the administrative practices, officials and skills of the settled societies they conquered, such as those of China and Iran.

To link the distant parts of the empire, they set up a swift relay system of couriers known as the yam. Riders carrying messages could change horses at regular stations, allowing news and orders to travel quickly across thousands of miles.
By keeping the trade routes such as the Silk Route safe, the Mongols encouraged commerce and the movement of goods and ideas across Eurasia.

answer: Thus efficient communication and trade held the empire together.

questions.q: What impact did the Mongol conquests have on trade and cultural exchange across Eurasia?

answer.text: though built by conquest, created conditions that boosted trade and exchange across Asia and Europe.

list: A single vast empire made the Silk Route safe, so goods, merchants and ideas moved freely over long distances
The Mongols set up a relay system of posts to speed messages and travellers

answer.text: The era saw wide cultural contact.

list: Technologies, religions and knowledge passed between China, Central Asia, West Asia and Europe
Travellers like Marco Polo journeyed across the empire, linking East and West as never before

questions.q: How is the image of Genghis Khan viewed differently in different traditions?

answer.text: is remembered in sharply different ways, depending on who tells the story.

list: To the settled peoples he conquered, he appears as a ruthless destroyer whose armies sacked cities and killed many
The written sources of these societies stress the violence of the invasions
He united the warring nomadic tribes and gave them law, unity and pride
In Mongolia today he is honoured as the father of the nation, showing how the same figure can be judged very differently
